log: Working out who would actually buy this
Rechecking product fit for the same audiences; market evidence is retained

Coverage gaps. Reddit, Indie Hackers and forum threads were requested repeatedly but the search layer returned mostly vendor blogs, comparison pages and SEO listicles; only one genuine community thread (Indie Hackers on wall-of-love placement) and one forum thread (BMF on course testimonials) surfaced, so direct buyer voice is thin across all seven candidates and the pain statements are largely inferred from practitioner and vendor writing rather than observed complaint. No purchase evidence was captured for any candidate — no pricing-page screenshots, no churn or switching accounts from named buyers. Searches that failed to yield usable evidence: BuiltWith technology-usage data for Senja widgets (no Senja entry surfaced, so no installed-base or site-level findability signal); LinkedIn Recommendations as a competing free alternative for solos (returned only how-to-write-a-recommendation content); local service businesses weighing Google Reviews against paid testimonial software (returned vendor pages, no buyer voice); Circle/Kajabi membership churn and testimonial practice (returned platform comparisons). Named organisation examples are weak: the only named users found are from Senja's own case studies and a review aggregator (New Media Summit, Modest, Makerbox, Creator Science), which are vendor-sourced and were not independently verified. Comparison claims about competitors in this map come from competitor-published pages and should be treated as marketing, not verified capability. Several source_urls are vendor or competitor marketing rather than buyer evidence; they are included because they document the workflow and the competitive field, and are flagged as such in each candidate's basis. Geography and language were unspecified and no boundary was imposed; all evidence found happens to be English-language.
7 audience(s) mapped; 1 worth exploring first. Commercial priority is a hypothesis, not a response-rate forecast.
